specs.name: 猫
specs.detail: Orange tabby cat with the EXACT original forehead and back stripes, cream muzzle/chest/toe tips, pink nose and ear interiors, glossy dark eyes and one upright curled tail with a cream tip. Four feline legs only. Locomotion is a natural eight-phase gentle quadruped walk: alternating front and rear paws with subtle shoulder/hip motion and a softly swaying single tail. Preserve the small original muzzle; do not turn it into a generic chibi cat.
specs.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: PetCast game animation sprite sheet for the EXISTING referenced pixel animal.
Input image 1 is the exact existing PetCast character and identity reference; it is not a generic style suggestion. Preserve its face, eye shape, proportions, silhouette, markings, palette and chunky pixel clusters, with no redesign.
Deliver one genuine transparent RGBA PNG sprite atlas, ideally 1536 x 1152 pixels. EXACTLY 4 equal columns and 3 equal rows: 12 separate full-body sprites in a strict invisible regular grid. Each cell is 384 x 384 pixels at that resolution. No drawn grid, no panel backgrounds, no labels, no numbers, no lettering, no watermark, no floor, no cast shadows and no extra objects.
All 12 characters must be the SAME individual at the SAME scale, facing the same RIGHT-FACING THREE-QUARTER direction as the reference, with a fixed camera and matching body/head registration. Every sprite, including ears/tail/fins, must be completely inside its own cell with at least 24 pixels of clear padding. Never clip or overlap cells.
Animation order is row-major: ROW 1 is a four-frame looping idle animation: neutral eyes open, a tiny breath with slight tail motion, a brief blink, return to eyes open. ROWS 2 and 3 together are a single EIGHT-FRAME looping locomotion cycle, four frames per row, continuing in temporal order. It is an in-place cycle: do not translate the whole animal across the sheet. The pose must actually change coherently, not eight identical stills. First and last phases must connect smoothly.
Pixel art only, matching the reference's detailed friendly game sprite aesthetic. Keep crisp square pixel steps, stable pixel size, restrained highlights, warm dark outlines and the original colors. Do not smooth into vector art, 3D or realistic painting. Maintain anatomical consistency in every frame.
